page: Microsoft Azure L48as_v4 is a member of the Lasv4 server family, utilizing a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 virtual CPUs, derived from 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 11,519 GB NVMe SSD, and the virtualization layer is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across multiple compute and memory metrics. The server achieves top 25% scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU evaluations, as well as in Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is notable for small-block read-only cached operations, which rank in the top 25%, though uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average category. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by hardware flags including AVX-512 and AES, reflected in strong Passmark encryption and extended instruction test scores.

While the server demonstrates high throughput for Redis SET operations and small-model LLM inference, it exhibits performance limitations on larger workloads. Specifically, text generation using a large 70B LLM model falls into the bottom 10% of benchmarks, indicating a clear tradeoff when attempting to run massive parameter models without dedicated GPU acceleration. Given the substantial 11.5 TB local NVMe storage and balanced memory-to-CPU ratio, this server is highly suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput caching layers, software compilation, and data-intensive general-purpose workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure L48as_v4 is an x86_64 server within the Lasv4 family, powered by a dedicated 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores. It features 384.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 11,519 GB NVMe SSD, managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the top 25% for multi-core CPU execution, software compilation, and Redis SET operations. However, uncached memory bandwidth and database operations perform at average levels, and text generation for large 70B LLM models falls into the bottom 10% due to the lack of GPU acceleration. This hardware profile makes the L48as_v4 highly effective for storage-heavy databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive general-purpose workloads, offering a strong balance of high-capacity local storage and dedicated compute resources.
